content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has developed a document titled Standards for Improving Quality of Maternal and Newborn Care in Health Facilities. This document outlines a comprehensive set of prioritized input, output, and outcome measures that can be utilized to define quality of care criteria and indicators. These measures are designed to align with locally agreed-upon targets to ensure relevance and applicability in various healthcare settings. In collaboration with the monitoring and evaluation teams from the WHO Department of Sexual and Reproductive Health and Research, as well as the WHO Department of Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health and Ageing, data on the implementation of these recommendations at both country and regional levels can be collected and assessed. This evaluation, conducted over the short to medium term, aims to determine the impact of these recommendations on national policies within individual WHO Member States. At the local level, information on recommended indicators can be gathered through methods such as interrupted time series analyses or clinical audits. In this context, the Guideline Development Group (GDG) has proposed specific indicators for consideration. One such indicator is the proportion of women undergoing cesarean sections who received alcohol-based chlorhexidine gluconate for skin preparation. This is calculated by dividing the number of women who received this antiseptic agent by the total number of women undergoing cesarean sections. Another indicator is the incidence of peripartum infections among women who had cesarean sections, calculated as the number of women with peripartum infections following cesarean delivery divided by the total number of cesarean deliveries. The first indicator evaluates the adherence to evidence-based practices among women at higher risk of infection during childbirth. The second indicator provides insights into the effectiveness of the intervention in preventing infections. WHO has also developed specific guidance for evaluating the quality of care for severe maternal complications, including sepsis, using the near-miss and criterion-based clinical audit approaches. The Executive Guideline Steering Group (GSG) convenes annually to review WHO’s portfolio of maternal and perinatal health recommendations. This group helps prioritize new and existing questions for recommendation development and updates. Recommendations are reviewed alongside others for prioritization, and if new evidence emerges that could impact the current evidence base, the recommendations may be updated. If no new evidence is identified, the recommendations may be revalidated. Following the publication and dissemination of updated recommendations, any concerns regarding their validity should be promptly communicated to guideline implementers, along with plans for further updates. WHO also welcomes suggestions for additional questions to be included in future updates. WHO has issued recommendations on the choice of antiseptic agents and methods of application for preoperative skin preparation in cesarean sections. These recommendations are based on systematic reviews and evidence synthesis, ensuring that they are grounded in the best available scientific data.
